title: The delete gate does not read a data heredoc's body as a command
intention: bin/cmd/deletegate removes the body of every here-document whose command is a data writer (cat or tee, optionally with redirects) before asking its two questions; a here-document fed to anything else (bash, sh, python, eval, ssh, ...) is kept and judged as today; the co-occurrence trade is otherwise unchanged.
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. This ticket closes live trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/deletegate-refuses-by-co-occurrence-across-clauses.json, a measured fault that enters as a bug (skills/intent/SKILL.md: a bug enters as a ticket, not through /intent). Measured 2026-10-08, n>=5: a `cat >> ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md <<'EOF'` whose prose contains the word rm is refused; the same append without the word is allowed; scratchpad probe scripts whose text mentions both are refused.
traces_to: Law 7 / CP4 (a gate whose false refusals cost more than a retype stops serving the work); Law 9 (measurement, n>=5, settles the trade the docstring recorded at n=2).
how: bin/cmd/deletegate verdict() (:110): before DESTRUCTIVE.search, strip data heredoc bodies with one regex pass: for each `<<-?\s*['"]?(\w+)['"]?` whose preceding command word on that line is cat or tee, drop the lines up to the matching terminator. Update the docstring's trade paragraph with the 2026-10-08 measurement and this narrowing, keeping the rest of the trade verbatim.

decisions.text: Narrow only the measured false positive (data heredocs to cat/tee); clause-splitting stays out, as the docstring's trade intended. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

deletegate gains _strip_data_heredocs(command) -> str, called at the top of verdict() and its result used for both questions. Over command.split('\n'): a line carrying <<-?\s*['"]?(\w+)['"]? is a data heredoc when the shell segment holding the << (the text before it after the last ; & | or ( on that line) has cat or tee as its first word AND the rest of the line after the heredoc word carries no | (a pipe onward runs it); then the following lines up to and including the terminator (the line equal to the word, leading tabs stripped for <<-) are dropped. No terminator found: nothing is dropped (judged as today). The command line itself is always kept. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Writing a script with a cat heredoc and running it later was never seen by this gate (a script file's text is not the command); stripping the body of a data heredoc does not widen that. The docstring's co-occurrence paragraph keeps its words and gains one paragraph: the 2026-10-08 measurement (n>=5, a cat >> ~/.cairn note whose prose said rm) and this narrowing to data heredoc bodies only. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py gained PROVES {'76d35575aead': {'1','2','3'}} and three teeth in its check list after the co-occurrence tooth: (1) three cat/tee data heredocs allowed; (2) bash, sh, python3 heredocs, a cat heredoc piped to bash, and an unterminated cat heredoc refused; (3) a plain guarded rm, an rm after a data heredoc, and an rm on the heredoc's own command line refused. Tooth 1 red-first 2026-10-11. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
